p.src: Now Cao Cao retreated as far as Xie Valley. Zhuge Liang, foreseeing that he would surely abandon Hanzhong and withdraw, dispatched Ma Chao and the other generals, dividing their forces among more than ten routes to raid him continually; thus Cao Cao could not remain there long. Moreover, after being struck by an arrow from Wei Yan, he hastily ordered the army home. The fighting spirit of the entire army was utterly spent. The vanguard had scarcely set out when fires arose on both sides: it was Ma Chao's ambush force in pursuit. Every man in Cao Cao's army lost heart. Cao Cao ordered his troops to hurry onward, racing day and night without pause; only when they reached Jingzhao did he finally feel secure.

p.src: Meanwhile, Xuande ordered Liu Feng, Meng Da, Wang Ping, and the others to seize Shangyong and its neighboring commanderies. When Shen Dan and the others heard that Cao Cao had abandoned Hanzhong and fled, they all surrendered. Once Xuande had pacified the people, he richly rewarded the whole army, to everyone's great delight. Thereupon all the generals conceived the desire to exalt Xuande as emperor; not daring to propose it to him directly, however, they went instead to report it to Military Adviser Zhuge. Zhuge Liang said, “I have already reached a decision on the matter.” He then led Fa Zheng and the others in to see Xuande and said, “Cao Cao now monopolizes power, and the people have no sovereign; my lord's benevolence and righteousness are renowned throughout the realm, and now that you possess both Chuan regions, you may answer Heaven's will and follow the people's desire by ascending the imperial throne. With your title thus rightful and your cause justified, you can punish the traitor to the state. The matter admits no delay; please choose an auspicious day at once.”

p.src: Greatly alarmed, Xuande said, “Your words are mistaken, Adviser. Though I, Liu Bei, belong to the imperial house of Han, I am still a subject; to do such a thing would be to rebel against Han.” Zhuge Liang said, “That is not so. The realm is now divided and crumbling, heroes are rising everywhere, and each holds sway over one region. The talented and virtuous men within the four seas who brave death and risk their lives in serving their lords all seek to attach themselves to a true sovereign and establish merit and fame. If my lord now clings to righteousness to avoid suspicion, I fear you will disappoint the hopes of all. I beg my lord to consider it carefully.” Xuande said, “If you would have me usurp that exalted station, I could never dare accept it. We may discuss some longer-term course instead.” The generals said with one voice, “If my lord does nothing but refuse, the hearts of the people will fall away.”

p.src: Zhuge Liang said, “My lord has made righteousness the foundation of his whole life and will not yet consent to assume the imperial title. But now that you possess Jingzhou, Xiangyang, and both Chuan regions, you may for the present become King of Hanzhong.” Xuande said, “Though you wish to honor me as king, to do so without an explicit edict from the Son of Heaven would be usurpation.” Zhuge Liang said, “At present we must act according to circumstance and not remain bound by ordinary principles.” Zhang Fei cried aloud, “Men not even of the imperial clan all wish to become rulers—how much more may my elder brother, who belongs to the house of Han! Never mind King of Hanzhong—what would be wrong with proclaiming yourself emperor?” Xuande rebuked him: “Say no more!” Zhuge Liang said, “My lord should adapt to circumstances and first advance to the rank of King of Hanzhong. It will not be too late afterward to submit a memorial to the Son of Heaven.”

p.src: After repeatedly declining but finding that he could not prevail, Xuande had no choice but to consent. In the seventh month of autumn, in the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an, an altar nine li square was built at Mianyang, laid out according to the five directions, with banners and ceremonial regalia erected in each. All the ministers took their appointed places in order. Xu Jing and Fa Zheng invited Xuande to ascend the altar. After presenting him with crown, robes, seal, and cord, they had him sit facing south, where he received the congratulations and obeisance of the civil and military officials as King of Hanzhong. His son Liu Shan was made heir apparent to the king. Xu Jing was appointed Grand Tutor, and Fa Zheng Prefect of the Masters of Writing. Zhuge Liang remained military adviser and assumed overall charge of the weighty affairs of army and state. Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, Zhao Yun, Ma Chao, and Huang Zhong were appointed the Five Tiger Generals; Wei Yan was made Administrator of Hanzhong. All the rest received ranks and titles according to their merits.

p.src: When the memorial reached Xudu, Cao Cao, then in Ye Commandery, learned that Xuande had proclaimed himself King of Hanzhong. In a fury, he cried, “How dare that whelp of a mat-weaver do such a thing! I swear I shall destroy him!” He immediately issued orders to muster every soldier in the realm and march on the two Chuan regions to settle the issue with the King of Hanzhong. One man stepped from the ranks and remonstrated: “Your Majesty must not, in a moment of anger, trouble yourself to lead a distant campaign in person. I have a plan that, without drawing a bow or loosing a single arrow, will cause Liu Bei to bring disaster upon himself in Shu; when his troops are weakened and his strength exhausted, a single general need only go against him, and success will be assured.” Cao Cao looked at the speaker and saw that it was Sima Yi. Delighted, Cao Cao asked, “What excellent counsel have you, Zhongda?” Sima Yi replied, “Sun Quan of the Southland married his sister to Liu Bei, who then took advantage of an opportunity to steal her back; while Liu Bei occupies Jingzhou and refuses to return it; each side therefore bears the other a bitter, gnashing hatred. You may now send an eloquent envoy with a letter to persuade Sun Quan to raise troops and seize Jingzhou. Liu Bei will surely send forces from the two Chuan regions to rescue it. At that moment, Your Majesty can raise an army to take Hanchuan. Unable to aid both front and rear, Liu Bei will inevitably be placed in peril.”

p.src: Cao Cao was overjoyed. He immediately wrote a letter, appointed Man Chong as his envoy, and sent him traveling through the night to the Southland to see Sun Quan. Learning of Man Chong's arrival, Sun Quan consulted his advisers. Zhang Zhao stepped forward and said, “Wei and Wu have never been enemies by nature; it was because we previously listened to Zhuge Liang's arguments that our two houses have fought year after year without cease, bringing ruin upon the common people. Now that Man Boning has come, he must intend to negotiate peace. We should receive him with courtesy.” Sun Quan followed his advice and ordered his advisers to escort Man Chong into the city for an audience. When the formalities were concluded, Sun Quan treated Man Chong with the courtesies due a guest. Man Chong presented Cao Cao's letter and said, “Wu and Wei have never been enemies; it is entirely because of Liu Bei that discord has arisen between them. The King of Wei has sent me here to arrange for you, General, to attack and seize Jingzhou while he brings his army against Hanchuan, striking Liu Bei from front and rear. After Liu Bei is defeated, we shall divide his lands between us and swear never to encroach upon each other.” After reading the letter, Sun Quan gave a banquet for Man Chong and then sent him back to the guest quarters to rest.

p.src: Sun Quan then consulted his advisers. Gu Yong said, “Though his words are persuasive, there is reason in them. For now, we may send Man Chong back on the one hand and arrange with Cao Cao to attack from front and rear; while on the other we send someone across the river to investigate Guan Yu's movements. Only then should we act.” Zhuge Jin said, “I have heard that after Guan Yu arrived in Jingzhou, Liu Bei arranged a marriage for him, and that his first child was a son and his second a daughter. The girl is still young and has not yet been betrothed. I am willing to go and seek her hand for my lord's heir. If Guan Yu agrees, we shall discuss with him how to join forces and defeat Cao Cao; if he refuses, we may then aid Cao Cao in taking Jingzhou.” Sun Quan adopted his plan and first sent Man Chong back to Xudu; then he appointed Zhuge Jin as envoy and sent him to Jingzhou. He entered the city, met Guan Yu, and exchanged the prescribed courtesies. Guan Yu asked, “Ziyu, what brings you here?” Zhuge Jin replied, “I have come especially to forge friendly ties between our two houses. My lord, the Marquis of Wu, has a son of remarkable intelligence. Having heard that you, General, have a daughter, I have come especially to propose a marriage. If our two houses unite in friendship, we can combine our strength to defeat Cao Cao. This would truly be an excellent affair. I beg Your Lordship to consider it.” Guan Yu flew into a rage and cried, “How could my tiger daughter ever marry a cur's whelp! Were it not for your brother's sake, I would behead you on the spot! Say no more!” He then summoned his attendants and had Zhuge Jin driven out.

p.src: Zhuge Jin fled in utter panic and returned to see the Marquis of Wu; not daring to conceal anything, he told him the truth. Sun Quan cried angrily, “How utterly discourteous he is!” He immediately summoned Zhang Zhao and the other civil and military officers to discuss a plan for taking Jingzhou. Bu Zhi said, “Cao Cao has long wished to usurp the Han throne, and the man he fears is Liu Bei; now he sends an envoy to make Wu raise troops and swallow up Shu. He means to shift the calamity onto Wu.” Sun Quan said, “I too have long wished to take Jingzhou.” Bu Zhi said, “Cao Ren now has troops stationed at Xiangyang and Fancheng. With no Yangzi to bar his way, he can take the overland route into Jingzhou. Why does he not seize it himself, but instead ask you, my lord, to mobilize? This alone reveals his intention. My lord should send an envoy to the capital at Xu to see Cao Cao and have Cao Ren first advance overland against Jingzhou. Guan Yu will surely draw off Jingzhou’s troops to attack Fancheng. Once Guan Yu moves, my lord may send a general to seize Jingzhou in secret, and it will fall at a single stroke.” Sun Quan followed his counsel, at once sending an envoy across the river to present Cao Cao with a letter explaining the plan. Cao Cao was delighted. He dismissed the envoy to return first, then sent Man Chong to Fancheng to assist Cao Ren as his adviser and discuss the deployment of troops; at the same time, he dispatched an urgent order to Eastern Wu, commanding it to send troops by water in support of the attack on Jingzhou.

p.src: Meanwhile, the King of Hanzhong ordered Wei Yan to take overall command of the troops and defend eastern Sichuan. He then led all his officials back to Chengdu. He appointed officers to construct a palace and establish lodging stations; from Chengdu to Baishui, more than four hundred lodges and post stations were built. He amassed grain and fodder and manufactured large quantities of weapons, intending to advance upon the Central Plain. Spies learned that Cao Cao had allied with Eastern Wu and intended to take Jingzhou, and they rushed the news into Shu. The King of Hanzhong hastily summoned Kongming to consult with him. Kongming said, “I had already foreseen that Cao Cao would devise such a scheme; yet Wu has many strategists, and they will surely advise him to make Cao Ren take the field first.” The King of Hanzhong said, “If that is so, what are we to do?” Kongming replied, “We can send an envoy to deliver Guan Yu’s patent of office and order him to strike Fancheng first. This will terrify the enemy’s troops, and they will naturally fall apart.”

p.src: The King of Hanzhong was delighted and immediately appointed Fei Shi, Major of the Vanguard, as envoy, sending him with the patent of appointment to Jingzhou. Guan Yu went beyond the city walls to welcome him and escorted him inside. When the formalities in the public hall were complete, Guan Yu asked, “What rank has the King of Hanzhong conferred on me?” Fei Shi replied, “First among the Five Tiger Generals.” Guan Yu asked, “Who are the five tiger generals?” . Fei Shi replied, “Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, Zhao Yun, Ma Chao, and Huang Zhong.” Guan Yu said angrily, “Yide is my younger brother; Mengqi comes from a renowned family of many generations; Zilong has long followed my elder brother and is as a younger brother to me. It is fitting that they should rank beside me. But what sort of man is Huang Zhong, that he should dare stand in the same rank as I? A true man will never consort with an old common soldier!” He therefore refused to accept the seal. Fei Shi smiled and said, “You are mistaken, General. In former days, Xiao He and Cao Shen joined Emperor Gaozu in his great undertaking and were his closest companions, while Han Xin was merely a defeated general of Chu; yet when Han Xin was elevated to the rank of king and placed above Xiao He and Cao Shen, no one ever heard that either bore him resentment for it. Now, though the King of Hanzhong has appointed five Tiger Generals, he is bound to you by the devotion of brothers and regards you as part of his own person. You, General, are the King of Hanzhong, and the King of Hanzhong is you. How could your standing be the same as that of the others? You have received the King of Hanzhong’s great favor and should share his joy and sorrow, his fortune and misfortune. You ought not to haggle over the relative heights of official titles. I beg you to consider this carefully.”

p.src: Guan Yu saw the truth and bowed twice, saying, “I was blind. Had you not instructed me, I would nearly have ruined a great undertaking.” He thereupon bowed and accepted the seal and cord of office. Only then did Fei Shi deliver the king’s command ordering Guan Yu to lead his forces against Fancheng. Guan Yu received the command and at once appointed Fu Shiren and Mi Fang as vanguard commanders, ordering them to lead a force ahead and encamp outside the walls of Jingzhou; meanwhile, he gave a banquet within the city to entertain Fei Shi. They drank until the second watch, when suddenly a report came that fire had broken out in the camp outside the city. Guan Yu immediately armed himself, mounted, and rode out to see. Fu Shiren and Mi Fang had been drinking, and a fire left unattended behind their tent had ignited the powder charges. Explosions shook the entire camp, and all the weapons, grain, and fodder were burned. Guan Yu led his men in fighting the blaze, which was not extinguished until the fourth watch.

p.src: Guan Yu returned to the city and summoned Fu Shiren and Mi Fang to rebuke them: “I appointed you two as the vanguard, yet before the army has even marched, you have burned so many weapons and provisions, while the explosions killed men and horses of your own command; if this is how you ruin affairs, what use have I for either of you?” He shouted an order to behead them. Fei Shi pleaded, “To execute senior generals before the army has even marched would be inauspicious for the troops. Their offense may be pardoned for the present.” Guan Yu’s anger had not abated. He shouted at the two, “Were it not out of regard for Major Fei, I would certainly cut off both your heads!” He then summoned guards to give each man forty strokes, stripped them of their vanguard seals and cords, and sentenced Mi Fang to guard Nanjun and Fu Shiren to guard Gong’an; and he added, “When I return victorious, if there has been the slightest mishap, I will punish both offenses together!” Their faces full of shame, the two murmured assent and withdrew. Guan Yu then appointed Liao Hua as vanguard and Guan Ping as deputy general. He himself commanded the central army, with Ma Liang and Yi Ji as staff officers, and they all set out together. Earlier, Hu Ban, son of Hu Hua, had come to Jingzhou and submitted to Lord Guan; remembering how Hu Ban had once saved him, Lord Guan was very fond of him. He ordered Hu Ban to accompany Fei Shi into Sichuan, there to see the King of Hanzhong and receive a title. Fei Shi took leave of Lord Guan and returned to Shu with Hu Ban.

p.src: Now on that day, after Lord Guan had offered sacrifice to the great commander’s banner, he dozed in his tent. Suddenly he saw a boar as large as an ox, black all over, charge into the tent and bite him directly on the foot. Guan Yu, furious, swiftly drew his sword and struck it, making a sound like the rending of silk. He awoke with a start and found it had been a dream, yet felt a dull ache in his left foot; deeply troubled, he called Guan Ping and told him the dream. Guan Ping replied, “The boar too bears the semblance of a dragon. A dragon attaching itself to your foot signifies soaring ascent. There is no need for misgivings.” Guan Yu assembled all the officers before his tent and told them of the portent in his dream. Some called it auspicious and others ominous; their opinions differed. Guan Yu said, “A true man nearing sixty years of age would have no regret even if he died!” While he was speaking, an envoy arrived from Shu bearing the King of Hanzhong’s decree appointing Guan Yu General of the Vanguard, granting him the imperial tally and battle-axe, and placing him in overall command of the nine commanderies of Jingzhou and Xiangyang. After Guan Yu had received the command, all the officers bowed their congratulations, saying, “This surely proves that the boar-dragon was an auspicious sign.” Guan Yu’s doubts were thus dispelled, and he raised his army and advanced along the main road toward Xiangyang.

p.src: Cao Ren was in the city when a sudden report came that Guan Yu himself was advancing at the head of an army. Cao Ren was greatly alarmed and wished to hold the city without coming forth. His deputy Zhai Yuan said, “The King of Wei has ordered you, General, to join Eastern Wu in taking Jingzhou. Now the enemy comes of his own accord to deliver himself to death. Why should you avoid him?” The adviser Man Chong remonstrated, “I have long known Guan Yu to be both brave and resourceful. We must not underestimate him. It would be best to hold firm.” The fierce general Xiahou Cun said, “That is merely the talk of a scholar. Have you not heard, ‘When water comes, dam it with earth; when a general comes, meet him with soldiers’? Our rested troops await a weary foe, so victory will naturally be ours.” Cao Ren followed his advice, ordering Man Chong to defend Fancheng while he personally led troops out to meet Guan Yu. p.src: Liao Hua rode out and challenged the enemy, and Zhai Yuan came forth to meet him. The two officers had fought only briefly when Liao Hua feigned defeat, wheeled his horse, and fled. Zhai Yuan pursued him from behind, and the Jingzhou troops retreated twenty li. The next day, he came again to offer battle. Xiahou Cun and Zhai Yuan both rode out to meet him, and once again the Jingzhou troops were defeated. After pursuing them for more than twenty li, they suddenly heard tremendous shouts behind them, while drums and horns sounded together. Cao Ren hastily ordered the vanguard to turn back, but Guan Ping and Liao Hua came attacking from the rear, throwing Cao's army into chaos. Realizing that he had fallen into a trap, Cao Ren first drew off one contingent and raced toward Xiangyang; but several li from the city, embroidered banners fluttered ahead, and Lord Guan sat reining in his horse, blade held crosswise, barring the road. Cao Ren, trembling with fear, dared not engage him and fled by a side road toward Xiangyang. Lord Guan did not pursue him. Presently Xiahou Cun's troops arrived. At the sight of Lord Guan, Xiahou Cun flew into a rage and engaged him; but in a single exchange, Lord Guan cut him down. Zhai Yuan fled, but Guan Ping overtook him and slew him with one stroke. Pressing their advantage, the victors pursued and attacked, and more than half of Cao's soldiers perished in the Xiang River. Cao Ren withdrew to defend Fancheng.

p.src: Having taken Xiangyang, Lord Guan rewarded his troops and reassured the people. Wang Fu, the army's assistant officer, said, “General, you took Xiangyang in a single assault, and though Cao's troops have lost heart, in my humble judgment Lü Meng of Eastern Wu, who has stationed troops at Lukou, has long harbored designs to annex Jingzhou. If he should lead his army straight against Jingzhou, how are we to withstand him?” Lord Guan replied, “I too have considered this. You may take charge of the matter: along both reaches of the river, at intervals of twenty or thirty li, choose elevated ground and erect a beacon tower. Station fifty soldiers to guard each tower. If the troops of Wu cross the river, signal by lighting fires at night and raising smoke by day. I shall go in person to strike them.” Wang Fu said, “Mi Fang and Fu Shiren guard the two strategic passes, but I fear they will not exert themselves fully. We must appoint another man to take overall command of Jingzhou.” Lord Guan said, “I have already assigned Administrative Officer Pan Jun to defend it. What is there to fear?” Wang Fu replied, “Pan Jun has always been suspicious of others and greedy for gain. He cannot be entrusted with the task. You should appoint Zhao Lei, the army's chief grain officer, in his place. Zhao Lei is loyal, honest, incorruptible, and upright. If you employ him, nothing can possibly go amiss.” Lord Guan said, “I have long known Pan Jun's character. Now that the appointment has been settled, there is no need to alter it. Zhao Lei now oversees the grain supplies, which is also an important responsibility. Do not indulge in needless doubts. Go and build the beacon towers as I have ordered.” Disheartened, Wang Fu bowed, took his leave, and departed. Lord Guan ordered Guan Ping to prepare boats to cross the Xiang River and attack Fancheng.

p.src: Now Cao Ren, having lost two officers, withdrew to defend Fancheng and said to Man Chong, “Because I did not heed your advice, my army has been defeated, my officers slain, and Xiangyang lost. What am I to do?” Man Chong replied, “Lord Guan is a tiger of a general, resourceful and full of stratagems. We must not underestimate him; our only course is to hold fast.” As they spoke, a man reported that Lord Guan had crossed the river and was coming to attack Fancheng. Cao Ren was greatly alarmed. Man Chong said, “We must simply hold fast.” The subordinate commander Lü Chang declared spiritedly, “Grant me several thousand troops, and I will meet the approaching army within the Xiang River.” Man Chong remonstrated, “You must not.” Lü Chang said angrily, “According to you civil officials, we should do nothing but hold fast. How can that repel the enemy? Have you not heard the maxim of the art of war: ‘Strike an army when half of it has crossed’? Lord Guan is now halfway across the Xiang River. Why should we not attack him? Once his troops reach the walls and his commanders approach the moat, it will be exceedingly difficult to withstand them.” Cao Ren immediately gave him two thousand troops and ordered Lü Chang to leave Fancheng and meet the enemy. When Lü Chang reached the river mouth, the embroidered banners ahead parted, and Lord Guan rode forth with his blade held crosswise. Lü Chang was about to advance and meet him. But the soldiers behind him, seeing Lord Guan's awe-inspiring might, fled before fighting, and Lü Chang could not halt them despite his shouts. Lord Guan charged in among them, cutting them down. Cao's army suffered a crushing defeat, losing more than half its cavalry and infantry. The defeated remnants fled into Fancheng, and Cao Ren hastily dispatched a messenger to seek aid. The messenger traveled through the night to Chang'an and presented Cao Cao with a letter saying, “Lord Guan has taken Xiangyang and is now pressing the siege of Fancheng with great urgency. We beseech you to send a great general to our rescue.”
